announced.description: A harness hook's pairing of an MCP tool call with the session making it, shared by every serving process until the result is reported.

call.description: the harness's tool use id, carried in the MCP message metadata

input_context.description: Historical context snapshot retained beside a transcript input for inspection; excluded from model requests.

items.description: Stored provider-neutral context items; an empty list records that no context was found.

ask.description: the model was asked here, from the prefix ending at `through`; what the provider keeps about it is stored in that provider's own component beside this one

through.description: the last entry of the prefix it was asked with

context_parts.description: where one model request's tokens went, beside its `usage`: each part of its context, and each large entry in it, with its tokens as they were paid (read from the provider cache, written to it, sent fresh, generated). The totals are the provider's; the split across parts is estimated from their sizes. The fixed part every request carries is one part, `fixed`, whose pieces are the session's `fixed`

parts.description: tokens by part: `fixed`, `input`, `notice`, `output`, `reasoning`, `checkpoint`, `call <tool>`, `result <tool>`, each as [read, write, fresh, generated]

entries.description: the same, for each entry of the context large enough to be named on its own, by its eid

fixed.description: what every model request of a session carries before its conversation, piece by piece in prompt order, each sized in characters: the harness's system prompt, each tool's schema, the instructions and each part of the persona, the skills, tools and agents it lists, and `unseen` for what its log never showed

parts.description: characters by piece: `system`, `tool <name>`, `persona <id>`, `instructions <file>`, `skills`, `mcp instructions`, `deferred tools`, `agent listing`, `unseen`

attempt.description: A provider request held while in flight; its state is computed from the holder and interruption mark. An unfinished dispatched request is ambiguous on restart.

state.description: The lifecycle derived from its interruption mark, holder and recorded answers.

by.description: the process or server holding the provider request

attention.description: an entry to be read before the next ask

hooked.description: on a session: its harness reports the tool calls of its own line of work to the hook door (POST /session/hook), where the bus says what the session is owed. Every context the harness runs shares the session’s id, so a tool reply never says it

brief.description: the session’s own account of itself, written at the end and quoted in the next one

cancel.description: an entry that withdraws an earlier one

seq.description: position of the last summarized entry, kept if that imported entry is later trimmed

overflow.description: the request refused for length that forced this checkpoint; only one compacted retry follows it

tasks.description: claimed task specifications frozen at this boundary, keyed by entity id

checkpoint.description: everything through this entry is settled: a compaction boundary

tasks.description: claimed task specifications frozen at this boundary, keyed by entity id

task_context.description: an admitted change to claimed task specifications, appended as passive context after its checkpoint; content carries the exact changes

claim.description: a session’s lock on the entity it is stored on

session.description: the session holding it — when that session’s entity dies the lock goes and the entity lives

at.description: when it was taken — stamped when the lock is new

task.description: a task a session holds is being worked on: a held claim reads `wip`, below the marks that end it

conflict.description: two sessions wanted one thing: written after the refusal, never by a client

loser.description: the session whose write was refused

holder.description: the session that already held the lock

dispatch.description: a child's place under the concurrency bound; settling removes it

state.description: Legacy compatibility during the dispatch marks expansion; removed after the deferred cutover.

entry.description: one entry of a transcript; the component stored beside it is its kind

seq.description: Positive integer position; omit on append to allocate atomically. Explicit fractional or occupied positions are refused.

fork.description: this session continues another transcript from one of its entries

from.description: the entry this fork continues from: the parent's entries up to it are this transcript's prefix

session.description: the session it is read into; when that session dies its transcript goes and the file stays

consumed.description: how many of its lines the importer has read; where a resume begins

version.description: file size and modification time of the immutable source being consumed; a changed version restarts its line cursor

finished.description: the immutable source version fully consumed after successful decoder EOF; its file size and modification time, so changed bytes reopen it

transcript.description: a file that holds a session's transcript, as the harness that ran it wrote it, and how far the importer has read it into the session. It sits on the file (@yaks/file), and each entry read from it wears the line it came from as `lines{file, start}`

notice.description: passive transcript context, included in the next ask without requesting one

task.description: the task that prompted this notice

reasoning.description: an entry the model reasoned with rather than returned

resume.description: set aside by an actor to come back to, with its place in the stack

session.description: a transcript something reacts to. Its chosen persona is kept here; what it is doing is read off its entries (`status`), where it runs is @yaks/process `process`, and what it was asked for is the `using` on its first entry

id.description: the runner’s own id for it

actor.description: who it speaks as — the identity that survives a /clear, where `created.via` is the run

source.description: the request that opened this transcript, when it has one

persona.description: the instructions chosen when this session began

transcript.description: the file it was first read from, whose entries are named by session and line alone; an entry read from any other file also names that file's path

operator.description: true for a transcript opened and driven by a person; false for an agent or automated opening, even if a person later replies

fallback.description: true for an MCP connection opened by the host's own process fallback, a request that named no caller; it speaks for nobody, and a door that trusts the host's perimeter may read it as the host's person (@yaks/harness conversations)

ended.description: this session is over: its harness ended it, its process is gone, or it came to rest with no process to ask about. What its entries leave unfinished reads stopped; settled, failed and empty read as they are. A resume or a message clears it

standing.description: a long-running session: recorded here rather than ended when its work is done

status.description: what the newest entry implies: pending is waiting on the model, running is waiting on an answer, settled has nothing to do

cost.description: the dollars its entries' `cost` records, summed; absent where none records any

spawned.description: a child session delegated by a parent; fork independently selects an inherited prefix

stop.description: on an entry, a marker ending the transcript; on a managed session, a request to stop its process

using.description: provider, model and effort: on an input it sets or switches them, on an ask it records what was served, and on a provider's row its model is what a request naming that provider alone runs

provider.description: the provider asked — kept as history when that entity is deleted, so a past ask still records what answered it

model.description: the model asked — kept as history when that entity is deleted, so a past ask still records what answered it

claim_take.title: Claim an entity
claim_take.description: Claim any entity for a session. Another session’s claim fails the batch; release it first. Reclaiming by the same session is a no-op refresh. Returns applied bundles.

claim_release.title: Release a claim
claim_release.description: Release any entity’s claim, unguarded to permit handover and recovery of dead sessions. Returns applied bundles.

session_context.title: Read a session’s context
session_context.description: Find/create a session and return its changes plus content.body identifying it and its claims for context injection. A hook cwd supplies the checkout persona when none is set. UserPromptSubmit instead returns timing from transcript_path, without writes: queued submissions supply sent time, otherwise hook time is labeled observed; unreadable transcripts return nothing. Explicit session overrides hook except for UserPromptSubmit. No session id means no writes or output.

session.description: Harness session id, human id or eid; overrides hook.

hook.description: JSON lifecycle event: hook_event_name, session_id, optional cwd. UserPromptSubmit adds transcript_path, prompt, optional prompt_id. CLI accepts stdin with -; MCP passes JSON text.

session_wrap.title: Wrap up a session
session_wrap.description: Save an optional brief and release session claims, except tasks parked on dependencies in managed runs. Returns applied bundles. An absent/unknown session makes no changes.

session.description: Harness session id, human id or eid; overrides hook.

hook.description: JSON lifecycle event with session_id; CLI accepts stdin with -.

session_listen.title: Listen for a session’s work
session_listen.description: Print one line for each thing addressed to an agent work session as it arrives: a comment on a stored record (entity) the session has claimed, or a person-written comment on one it created (the comment’s own created.via is not a session), a knock at the session or at that record, a letter delivered to it, a letter answering one it wrote, and a reply held for its project (also a person-written comment on a record filed there once its creating session ended): one answering a letter another session wrote, sent to the project the listening session works for (its persona’s home, or a project filed under it) after that other session ended. Each item is marked notified once printed, so it is printed once, including anything that arrived while nothing was listening; the session’s own writes are never printed. Meant for a command line under a monitor that reads each printed line as an event, such as Claude Code’s Monitor tool: `yak session listen --session "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"`, which does not return while the process is up. With once, it waits until something is addressed to the session, prints it and ends, for a harness that wakes its agent when a background command ends, such as Claude Code’s background Bash: `yak session listen --session "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID" --once`, run again each time it ends. A printed line counts as heard, so its output must reach the agent itself, never a file.

session.description: the session to listen for (default: the caller’s session); pass its id or registered name

once.description: end after the first read that prints anything, instead of listening until the process stops

session_brief.title: Record a session’s brief
session_brief.description: Replace a session brief, creating a missing named transcript. session overrides hook.session_id, then defaults to caller. Returns the written bundle; does not inject context elsewhere.

session.description: Harness session id, human id or eid; overrides hook.

hook.description: JSON lifecycle event with session_id; CLI accepts stdin with -.

hooks_install.title: Install the lifecycle hooks
hooks_install.description: Install Claude-compatible lifecycle hooks: session/subagent start reads context, prompt submission adds transcript timing, and session end wraps up. PreToolUse posts MCP calls to the server for session attribution; PostToolUse delivers notifications to the parent agent. Transcript import supplies intervening turns. Replaces this install’s hooks, preserving unrelated settings. Writes on this machine; returns the settings path. remove uninstalls these hooks.

claim_check.title: Check for stale claims
claim_check.description: Report claims held by missing, stopped or failed sessions in content.body, including warning/failure findings. Does not repair.

session_cache.title: Report prompt-cache observations
session_cache.description: Report input-token-weighted cached share by session, provider, model and derived path. Uses request created.at in [from, until). Share is sum(cached_tokens)/sum(input_tokens) over requests reporting both counts; missing counts are unknown, not zero. Reports unknown coverage and explicit zero-cache requests. No date bounds reads all history. Returns JSON in content.body and output.value; no stored rollup. Imported CLI entries (even with ask) and usage-only entries may be cumulative turn totals: excluded from total and session/provider/model groups, counted in imported_observations and shown separately in groups.path.imported.

from.description: inclusive ISO instant with timezone, e.g. 2026-10-01T20:10:00Z

until.description: exclusive ISO instant with timezone, e.g. 2026-10-01T20:10:00Z

session.description: only this session; pass its id or registered name

requests.description: include individual request ids, times, counts and shares

session_check.title: Check for stalled sessions
session_check.description: Report sessions waiting beyond the stall threshold (default two hours) in content.body. Does not repair: the transcripts duty ends a session whose process is gone.

session_input.description: an input line inherits its transcript's selected model and owes one turn; an entry selecting a model is already owed by session_run

session_run.description: advance a transcript by one independently owed step: a `using` on an entry asks for a turn, a result or a Pending entry (a background call that outlasted its patience) is something new for the model to read, a cancel withdraws the request in flight, a stop ends it (and gives up a child's place), a child is admitted, or a task a transcript holds completes, is cancelled or loses a dependency (a `requires` or `contains` link going, read by the ends it had). A model request the provider failed but may yet answer is asked again after the pool's backoff, eight tries in a row at most

session_release.description: release claims held by a transcript that stopped or failed, except those a managed run that ended cleanly is parked on: a task still waiting on a dependency, or any while a request waits for its next run. A parked task finishing lets its claim go. Runs recorded with terminal marks are claimed by the next worker even when no worker was serving effects

session_wake.description: wake every transcript parked on a task that waits on the one that finished, or on a task whose link to an unfinished dependency went away (a `requires` or `contains` edge going, read by the ends it had): where its run is over, an input carrying the `using` in force asks for its next turn, which whoever answers that provider runs (the session runner, or @yaks/spawn for a command line)

native.description: A transcript run by the native model/tool loop, not an outside CLI agent.

tool_async.description: a native transcript call dispatched by its own durable effect; no session lease waits for it, and a request answers it with a derived Pending until its result lands

tool_progress.description: the Pending entry of a background call that outlasted its patience: an immutable interim result that is something new for the model to read, so it may take a turn while the call runs; older transcripts hold one beside every background call

session_tool.description: execute one asynchronous native tool call independently of the session lease; the tools runner owns its execution claim and final result

sending.description: what is sent to a model: selected on an input, recorded on an ask

input.description: explicit model-native inputs, such as lyrics or duration; validated by the provider, never inferred from the prompt

instructions.description: system instructions in force for this transcript

window.description: how many of the transcript's newest entries a turn sends the model, reaching back to the input that began the turn they cut into; the whole transcript where absent

tools.description: the tools a turn is offered, by name: exactly these, from every tool the runner can run; the runner's own set where absent
